items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: So at that time “So What,” “Kind of Blue” by Miles Davis had been out two years. And I’d been experimenting with modal songs. So one day, there was a piano in the room, I said — thirty minute lessons — and we had about ten minutes to go. I said, “Susan, I want you to play me the D minor scale... So

ctx.x: Students don’t have that now, so I don’t know if there’s any conclusion about that because certainly jazz is part of almost all music school curriculums, but we’ll get there. We’ll come back to that. Did you have an aha moment, sort of an epiphany along the way about what you do? How did this launch, this idea of people can learn to improvise and I can help them?

Yeah. I’m glad you asked me that because I have, the lady that helped me get this started, her — I think her address is over on my thing and I almost wrote her a letter. I’ve been waiting since — I’ve been waiting over 60 years to write her a letter. When I was in college I told everybody I wouldn’t be a teacher because some of the students that I heard practicing in the rooms next to me and the recitals that I had to go to, I didn’t think they played their instrument very well. So back then I was very naïve. I…

a teacher you had to really play well, because you’re going to be an example. So I told everybody I wouldn’t be a teacher. But yet when I got up to about my fourth year, senior year, I was out in the parking lot, it might have been my junior year in the spring. And Gene Montooth comes up to me and he at the time had a goatee and he was what we would call a hippie. Played tenor, okay? Played oboe, maybe bassoon I can’t remember. But he came up and said, “Hey Jamey, I’ve got a job teaching in the fall, high school.…
